## North star (quoted from `.syzygy/governance/doctrine/vision.md`)
- "Showing the truth is the soul of the product."
- Owner's words: "open one place, understand what a project's vision and goals are, tune or guide
  them if necessary, and know that the rest of the project will (eventually) mold itself to fit
  around that goal."
- VIS-1 ordering: (1) truth and observation determinism; (2) comprehension of the truth's
  presentation; (3) momentum; (4) breadth/fidelity; (5) reproducibility of derived convenience.
  "Comprehension is achieved by simplifying presentation, never content."
- VIS-2: no evidence means Unknown, never success. VIS-3: every normative artifact stays digestible
  by a human unfamiliar with the project. VIS-7: every rendered internal link resolves; every
  encoding means what its legend says; no secret material on any surface.

S3-architecture-diagrams.gap: The architecture diagrams are careful, well-tested craft within a narrow, self-imposed vocabulary: renderPolarisMarkdown's flow/relations fences (polaris-markdown.ts:108-127) are pure, escaping-safe, 0-svg, and every rendered node in the capture (19/19) carries real source provenance with a genuine text-equivalent explanation drawn from the same evidence span ("Read the diagram explanation"), correctly mount-prefix-aware citation links, and no fragment-in-<details> trap. It falls short of world-class on four independent axes. First, the diagram vocabulary can only express a strict linear chain or a flat bag of independent from/to pairs -- no fan-in/fan-out, hierarchy or cycle is representable, so real many-to-one structure (the connectors figure) is compressed into three generic linear boxes, folding away which named systems exist. S6-machine-parity.label: S6-machine-parity
S6-machine-parity.gap: The machine side of the two-first-class-consumers doctrine has never been engineered as a contract: `/api/poc`'s handler is exactly `JSON.stringify(model)` (routes.ts:159-162, confirmed verbatim by the parity test's own comment at polaris-parity-sweep.test.ts:4-6), so the 'machine-queryable endpoint' is the internal PocModel dumped whole, with no query parameter honored (machineHandle takes no `request` at all), no pagination, no field selection, no ETag/Cache-Control/compression negotiation (server.ts respond() sets only content-type), and no self-link from `/api/poc` to its own sibling `/api/poc/polaris` presentation endpoint or any human route -- a fresh agent holding one URL and a Bearer token cannot discover the second endpoint exists, and no JSON-Schema/OpenAPI document exists anywhere in the repo for either shape (the only self-description is a bare version string, 'schema': 'syzygy-three-surface-poc/v1'). Where the payload does declare a richer vocabulary it does not deliver: the presentation endpoint's narrative enumerates six anchor target classes (doctrine, contract, requirement, decision, evidence, work) and three block roles, but the live capture uses exactly one role for all 714 blocks and only 3 of 6 classes across 916 anchors -- 914 evidence, 1 requirement, 1 work, zero doctrine/contract/decision -- so the machine narrative is, empirically, the same Butlers-shape evidence the human page renders, not the doctrine/intent layer the owner's north star names ('open one place, understand what a project's vision and goals are'). What is solid: credential admission is centralized, timing-safe and deliberately silent on failure detail (credentials.ts:270, server.ts:188-200, RFC5-3), the response ceiling is enforced identically for both channels via one `boundedResponse` (routes.ts:137-142), the underlying PocModel data is genuinely rich (per-claim epistemic labels, provenance, digests) and a real independent parity oracle exists (polaris-parity-sweep.test.ts) that compares dozens of marker families between rendered HTML and parsed machine JSON as multisets against a 7x6 fixture-state matrix -- a bar well above ad hoc spot-checking. The gap to ideal is structural, not a missing feature: one versioned, self-describing, queryable machine contract from which both the human page and the presentation endpoint are pure projections, with parity a property of that shared contract rather than something re-verified sweep by sweep.

S7-pwb-pipeline-core.label: S7-pwb-pipeline-core
S7-pwb-pipeline-core.gap: As engineering, the PWB pipeline (body-read-authority -> project-shape-observation -> git-object-reader -> content-classification -> project-shape-extraction -> project-shape-coverage -> project-shape-model.ts) is disciplined: no wall-clock or Math.random anywhere in the eight core stage modules [Observed, grep clean], every unordered collection (Map/Set) is sorted before use (project-shape-manifest.ts:322-324,515; project-shape-coverage.ts:268; git-object-reader.ts:218) so the shape is derivable from (Butlers commit, observer version) alone as the north star wants; project-shape-coverage.ts commits in its own header comment to 'nothing here ever drops a declaration or hard-codes a winner' and walkthrough-readiness.ts evaluates every one of its ten arms as a sweep rather than stopping at the first failure so the owner sees every reason at once (walkthrough-readiness.ts:17-18,272-367); and test density is roughly 1:1 to 1:1.5 lines of test to source across the nine-class extraction grammar (1128/818), coverage reconciliation (650/593) and observation stage (886/650). Against that, three specific mechanisms fall short of the honesty bar this audit was asked to weigh. First, and most concrete: extraction amplifies one class's grammar failure into the loss of OTHER, independently-successful classes from the very same source, and this is a deliberate, spec-quoted and unit-tested choice, not an oversight (project-shape-extraction.ts:14-17 'A source never yields a partial item set'; extractSource's loop at :638-650 discards `all` the moment any class fails; project-shape-extraction.test.ts:778-786 constructs a vision.md fixture where the comment itself says 'project-account-section and success-criterion would succeed alone' yet asserts the whole source still reports 'unknown'). v1.md alone carries three unrelated classes this way (project-shape-manifest.ts:250: project-account-section + success-criterion + catalog-entry), so the real-world v1.md whole-source-Unknown already in LEDGER.md is, mechanically, at least three facts being wiped by one. Second, the nine-class extraction grammar enumerates a CLOSED, hardcoded set of expected headings (CATALOG_HEADINGS, project-shape-extraction.ts:56-66) and only ever asks 'is each of the nine present exactly once'; a Butlers edit that ADDS a tenth v1.md catalog category is neither extracted nor flagged — it produces no failure, no Unknown, no denominator entry, just silence, which is a narrower instance of the silent-wrong class VIS-2 forbids (distinct from L1's tree-only-rule and seeded-entity instances: this one lives inside the grammar dispatch itself, extractCatalogEntries at :438-460). Third, the resource ledger (resource-ledger.ts) is structurally input-side only: its two limits are maxTotalBytes (bytes read) and maxParsePassesPerSource (traversals charged), and its ResourceLedgerSummary (:81-90) has no field that could hold a served/output byte count — so wiring it to the already-known response-ceiling breach (P0-CEILING) is not a call-site fix but a new counter the registry envelope does not yet declare. None of the three findings contradicts the pipeline's honesty commitments elsewhere; they are the places where a genuinely careful design chose whole-population conservatism or has not yet been asked to own a boundary, and the ideal — the whole-source Unknown narrowed to whole-class Unknown per independent class, a closed-vocabulary grammar that also detects what it does not recognize, and one budget owning both input read and output served bytes — is close and mechanically specified below.

S8-renderer-modules.label: S8-renderer-modules
S8-renderer-modules.gap: The renderer is disciplined where it matters most (every free-text interpolation in polaris.ts eventually passes through the shared @syzygy/cap1-daemon escapeHtml before it reaches the page, and the module decomposition is real: 8 focused files plus a 274-line declared copy table). But it is not yet a projection whose size is bounded by design: one 1,615-line god-module (polaris.ts, 89 top-level functions, one 265-line function) carries the entire page, and at the current Butlers evaluation, 49.4% of the 2,090,025-byte capture (1,032,964 bytes) is machine-metadata payload -- a 625,232-byte embedded narrative-JSON blob plus 407,732 bytes of near-identical claim-tuple attribute spans -- not human prose. Most of that metadata is either provably constant across the page (one evaluation id repeated 699 times) or repeated per-leaf-node when it could be inherited from an ancestor (two static compliance flags stamped on 2,615 elements). The escape discipline itself is 100% convention -- no branded HtmlString type, no lint rule -- so it is one careless new call site away from breaking, and the one dated mutation-kill run that covers polaris.ts is bound to a SHA-256 the file no longer matches, having gone through a byte-ceiling trim and two feature PRs since. The frozen reading-plan/narrative data is hand-authored with no generator, which L1 already flags for portability; here the same fact means the presentation layer has no reproducible build path from source to bytes -- a human types offsets once and the renderer trusts them forever.

S9-generation-kit.surface: generation kit and authoring path (operator view)
S9-generation-kit.gap: Judged as an operator recipe -- 'open one place, follow it, get a validated draft' -- the kit is a well-written, well-hedged reading (AUTHORING.md's writing guidance is genuinely good, and every doc correctly disclaims candidate status) wrapped around a path that breaks or dead-ends at nearly every step. No real, non-Butlers worked example exists anywhere in the kit: the only runnable second-project evidence hard-scripts every stage response and proves orchestration, not authoring or portability. An operator unfamiliar with Syzygy, working only from the kit, cannot get from a new repository to a validated draft preview today -- and would be actively misled about what the schema accepts.

S10-operability.label: S10-operability
S10-operability.gap: As the owner's instinctive first stop, the daemon nails cold start (one command, a clear stdout banner naming URL/repo/revision/credential path, fail-closed on a missing repo, unbound credential, or a dirty Syzygy checkout) and the home page's footer does carry Butlers commit, working-tree digest, observer commit and as-of instant (routes.ts:92) — so 'what am I serving, from which commits, how old' is technically answerable from one already-open page. Everything past that first minute is a blank. There is no status/health route anywhere in the app or the shared daemon package (grep of both source trees for health/status/ready routes returns nothing outside test fixture text) — VIS-1's promised comprehension of the machine plane does not extend to the daemon's own operating state. server.ts logs nothing per request: the captured daemon.log from this run's own orchestrator (scratchpad/capture/daemon.log) holds exactly the one-time startup banner despite ~10 requests having been served against it (curl calls in run.sh) and daemon.err is empty throughout — a 401 credential refusal, a 404, a 500 handler failure, or the already-recorded P0-CEILING 503 leave no trace anywhere but the HTTP response itself, so an operator who was not the client of the failing request cannot discover it happened. Where structured failure detail does exist (DaemonStart's three failure arms all carry a `.detail` string), main.ts drops it before it reaches the operator: `daemon did not start (${start.failure.kind})` prints only the arm name, so a real port collision reads as the bare word 'bind-failed' with no 'address already in use' or port number, and an unprovisionable credential prints without its state-write-boundary reason. The Syzygy observer's own commit is never printed unconditionally — it only reaches the terminal indirectly, embedded in the walkthrough-binding lines, which print only when PWB-REQ-022's governance inputs load. The target Butlers repository's own working-tree cleanliness is computed (git-observation.ts:60-82, `clean`/`changedPaths`) and then read nowhere outside its own module — an uncommitted Butlers tree silently folds into an opaque sha256 digest with zero operator-visible warning, even though the observer's own checkout gets exactly this check (`pocObserverInputsAreClean`) wired to a named, fail-closed startup error. Restart/upgrade has no story at all: no systemd unit, no wrapper script, and docs/THREE-SURFACE-POC.md's four sections (fresh checkout, walkthrough, evidence capture, absences) never mention restarting, upgrading the observer, or picking up a new Butlers commit — the only documented lifecycle is SIGINT/SIGTERM to a foreground process the operator is already watching. Ideal: one status route (human and machine) stating what is running, from which commits, how stale, what degraded and why, reachable without already knowing a URL scheme; every failure surfaced by that route or by a structured stderr line, never only inside a response body nobody but the failing client sees; and a documented, scripted restart = pick-up-new-commits-with-nothing-lost story.

S11-visual-language.label: S11-visual-language
S11-visual-language.gap: The visual language gets the load-bearing basics right and then stops short of being a system. The shared token set (design-tokens.ts:43-156) gives every computed foreground/background pair on the dark palette AA-or-better contrast (muted-on-void 7.23:1, muted-on-panel 6.79:1, notice text 12.6:1, measured this session), the responsive breakpoints at 999px/800px/640px genuinely restructure the reading layout rather than just reflowing text, and the disclosure population (0 of 353 <details> open by default, polaris.ts:339 comment 'coverage counts stay available on demand, never as the default view') is a deliberate, working density strategy. But VIS-7's 'every encoding means what its legend says' is the doctrine this surface exists to satisfy, and outside the two-state Observed/Unknown pill that L6 already audited, it fails on its own terms: the claim-state glossary that polaris-copy.ts:30-52 declares (7 tiers, 4 freshness values, 1 challenge value -- 12 states beyond label) renders through exactly one CSS rule, .claim-tuple (polaris.ts:1296-1299,1375), with zero attribute selectors keyed on any of the data-epistemic-tier/-freshness/data-challenge-state values the markup already carries (polaris.ts:315) -- so 699 claim-tuple spans in the capture are pixel-identical grey monospace regardless of whether they say gate-backed or suspended, fresh or broken. The one glossary that explains those states (polaris.ts:347-353) is a single collapsed <details> reachable by aria-describedby, so even a sighted reader who wants the key must find and open it once and hold twelve definitions in their head while scanning identical text. Layered on top, the palette's few colors are reused for unrelated meanings with no legend covering the reuse: --unknown backs both 'no evidence' (the epistemic pill) and 'proposed OpenSpec change, not current authority' (polaris.ts:1309-1310), a state that is not evidentiary at all, at a contrast of 1.11:1 from the separately-named --amber already used elsewhere on the page -- the two tokens are visually one color; --cyan backs 'Observed' on Polaris, 'mapped code region' on Orrery (orrery.ts:54-55) and 'the one work item this POC demonstrated' on Trajectory (trajectory.ts:130-131), three unrelated referents, none registered in the one legendHtml() component every page renders (page-shell.ts:67,70). Underneath both problems is the same root cause: there is no design system, only accreted component CSS. Spacing has four named tokens; typography has none -- 35 distinct ad hoc font-size declarations across the four style blocks, several within .02-.04rem of each other with no visible rationale -- and 8 raw hex colors appear directly in component rules outside the 10 declared custom properties, at least one of which (#102126) duplicates an existing token's exact value byte-for-byte while bypassing it. A reader cannot sense truth-state before reading a word, because most of the truth-states the product itself defines were never given a visual state to be sensed.

L1-portability.label: L1-portability
L1-portability.surface: Polaris rendering/observation stack (packages/three-surface-poc-core PWB pipeline + apps/three-surface-poc renderer)
L1-portability.gap: The pipeline's architecture is already portable and its content is not. Every stage is pure, injectable and parameterized where it matters — the git runner, the resource ledger, the secret policy, the body-read authority evaluation and the nine walkthrough answer identities are all project-neutral, and body-read-authority validates consent, policy and registry documents generically. But every project-specific value is a TypeScript const with a test asserting byte-equality against the governed artifact that already holds it: the root index path, five pillar keys and labels, the per-basename extraction bindings, the Butlers heading literals, the nine catalog keys, the seven precedence rows down to 'src/, alembic/, tests/', the class-to-layer table (restated in four places), the page's h1, its tagline and all six remediation routes, and the approved repository locator as one user's absolute home directory. The registry entry is used as a checksum, not as a source, so amending it changes nothing at runtime and 'change the project' means editing five core modules plus the renderer and re-authoring their conformance expectations. Pointed at Syzygy itself the stack mostly fails closed and honestly — the root index is absent, all five pillars go Unknown — which is the right behaviour and the reason this is weak rather than broken. Two paths do not fail closed: the tree-only population rules run regardless of whether the root index read, so any OpenSpec-shaped repository yields modeled baseline-spec counts beneath a wholly unread shape; and the PocModel's seeded Butlers entities feed Trajectory and Orrery with no digest to catch the mismatch. Both are the silent-wrong class VIS-1 ranks worst. The distance to 'change the project means change one profile input' is one structural move (M1) that the governed artifacts are already shaped to receive, three small truth repairs (M3, M4, M7), and a measurement (M5) that is available today without any new consent act.

findings.title: The registry already carries the per-project grammar as data, but the code holds hard-coded copies and the tests assert byte-equality — the registry is a checksum, not a source
findings.note: The act-bound registry entry declares observationGrammar.fixedCatalogKeys, rootSummary, precedence.rows and factFamilyRows; the policy declares sourceAdmission.phaseA.fixedSeedPaths. Every one of those values also exists as a TypeScript const, and the module headers state the design intent explicitly ('hard-coded copies of the act-bound registry entry; the test proves them byte-equal'). Consequence: a second project's registry entry changes nothing at runtime. 'Change the project' means editing five core modules and re-authoring their conformance expectations.

findings.title: Tree-only population rules 3 and 4 run even when the root index never read — a second project can emit modeled facts beneath a wholly Unknown shape
findings.note: BASELINE_SPEC=/^openspec\/specs\/([^/]+)\/spec\.md$/ and ROSTER_BUTLER=/^roster\/([^/]+)\/butler\.toml$/ are applied over the whole tree unconditionally, outside the pillar block and with no dependence on rootIndex.state. Point the observer at any repository that uses OpenSpec's conventional layout and it mints baseline-spec items keyed by directory name while all five pillars report 'root-index-missing-at-revision'. Degradation is recorded, but the class aggregate for baseline-spec is genuinely modeled: the page shows real counts for a project whose declared shape was never read. This is the silent-partial-truth class, the worst failure under VIS-1.

findings.title: The page's project identity — heading, tagline, every remediation route — is literal copy, never derived from the observed repository
findings.note: 'Butlers' appears 96 times in the rendered capture. The h1 carries data-copy-role="project-fact" (softened by data-claim-role="non-normative-framing" and data-non-citable), and 'Less to remember. More room to live.' is the observed project's own tagline carried as a scope-instruction with no anchor at all — so no anchoring rule and no parity sweep can catch it. Repointed at a second repository the page asserts the wrong project's name over the right project's facts, and every Unknown's route instructs the reader to repair the file 'in Butlers'.

findings.title: The seven precedence rows are compared against hard-coded literal prose, so no second project can ever adjudicate a contradiction
findings.note: extractPrecedenceTable requires an H3 spelled exactly 'Precedence Order When Layers Disagree', four columns, seven rows, and each Layer/Owns/Home cell equal to a LAYER_ROWS literal — including 'about/heart-and-soul/', 'roster/{butler}/' and 'src/, alembic/, tests/'. expandedHomes then detects the roster template and the inert row by string equality against ROSTER_HOME_TEMPLATE and INERT_HOME. A second project cannot supply a precedence table at all, so every contradiction stays 'contradicted-pending-adjudication' forever. Honest, but the whole adjudication capability is dead on arrival off Butlers.

findings.title: The approved repository locator is one user's absolute filesystem path, compiled into the app
findings.note: PWB_APPROVED_REPOSITORY_LOCATOR = '/home/tze/GitHub/butlers'. The registry's own inputClasses already names 'repository-locator-mapping' with identityScheme 'opaque-repository-id-plus-normalized-approved-locator' — the governed input exists and the code does not read it. Consequence beyond portability: the daemon refuses any other --repo, so a repaired Butlers page cannot be measured from a scratch clone (already a known measurement constraint), and no second project can be bound without a source edit and rebuild.

findings.title: The extraction grammar dispatches on file basename, and a second project can share Butlers' basenames with different meanings
findings.note: Classes are assigned by (pillar, path-relative-to-root) and parsed by basename: vision.md / architecture.md / v1.md / components.md / README.md. Syzygy's own .syzygy/governance/doctrine/ holds vision.md, architecture.md and v1.md — identical basenames, different ontology. Most rules would fail closed on the Butlers heading literals ('What Butlers Is', 'Key Architectural Facts', the nine catalog H3s) and yield Unknown, which is honest. The exception is extractProjectAccountSections for architecture.md, whose rule is content-free (concatenate every H2), so it would succeed on a foreign architecture.md and publish that text under Polaris's 'Architecture' framing as a modeled project-account fact.

findings.title: One five-pillar ontology is hard-coded in four independent places that must agree
findings.note: PILLAR_KEYS/PILLAR_LABELS (manifest), extractionClassesFor (manifest), CLASS_ROWS class->layer-ordinal (coverage) and classesForPillar (model) each restate the same Butlers layer model. Changing a project means keeping four tables consistent by hand with no single schema that says they must be; a mismatch does not fail loudly, it shifts which pillar's Unknown is reported.

findings.title: The authority expectations are a singleton for one repository, one policy version and one act triple
findings.note: pwbAuthorityExpectations() returns one Record<AuthorityKind,...> naming repository:butlers-configured-poc, policyVersion 1.1.0-candidate.1 and three literal act identities/phrases; PWB_REPOSITORY_ID is a const; the snapshot identity is built as `butlers:${revision}`. The body-read-authority module itself is genuinely project-neutral (it parses consent/policy/registry documents and validates identities by regex) — the coupling is entirely in this one wiring layer, which is good news: it is the cheapest thing here to key by repository id.

findings.title: The frozen reading plan is 310 lines of byte offsets into one Butlers file, imported unconditionally by the renderer
findings.note: Fails safe: applyReadingPlan re-hashes the statement and returns the full declaration on any mismatch, so a second project silently loses condensation and the ten component guides rather than mis-attributing spans. The portability cost is structural, not epistemic — the figures, chapter ids ('architecture-daemon', 'architecture-mcp', ...) and titles ('How the outside world reaches Butlers') are application source, so a second project's reading plan is a source edit.

The builder is literally buildButlersPocModel. L2-owner-core-loop.label: L2-owner-core-loop
L2-owner-core-loop.surface: Polaris (/polaris) judged as the owner's core daily loop: cold-open -> notice -> tune -> dispatch -> land -> account
L2-owner-core-loop.gap: Judged only as the owner's daily loop -- cold-open, notice, tune, dispatch, watch it land, close the day with an account -- Polaris is world-class at step 1 and absent from steps 2-6. The cold open satisfies PWB-REQ-010 honestly: seven project-level groups before any capability detail, every positive claim anchored, every Unknown stated in place with a named route. Then the loop stops. The 2,087,400-byte page carries 1,061 links, of which exactly one reaches /trajectory (the global nav), zero <form> elements, and a single <button> that expands a disclosure. The page itself renders `relationship:intent-to-work` as "Unknown -- The human-triggered materialization step has not run" and offers no way to run it, while the action that would (POST /trajectory/materialize) sits one surface away, hard-coded to one pre-chosen Butlers requirement the owner never selected anywhere. The owner's only other named lever, "Policy change by the owner, or accept the exclusion" over 12 excluded-content claims, is prose inside a <details> in the last h3 of the last h2. Nothing records that the owner disagrees (VIS-6a is wholly unimplemented: zero occurrences of annotation, dismissal or .syzygy/local across both POC trees and cap1-core), and nothing is retained between evaluations (the state dir holds only the machine credential; asOf is `new Date()` at build time), so "what changed since I last looked" is unanswerable by construction. Doctrine's own falsifier is exact: "A Syzygy from which no work is ever dispatched has failed, regardless of how good its documents look" (vision.md:61-64). The documents are very good. The loop is one nav link wide. Tier is weak rather than broken only because the single action does exist, works, and is idempotent -- it is simply unreachable from the surface where the owner forms the intent.

L3-generation-loop.label: L3-generation-loop
L3-generation-loop.gap: Judged as a product loop, the landed generator is a superb bounding layer wrapped around a hole where the honesty contract should be. What landed is real and project-neutral: 892 non-test lines with zero project proper nouns, a canonical JSON encoder and a hand-written bounded parser that reject duplicate keys, proxies, custom prototypes and __proto__ keys; a six-stage controller that races cancellation and deadline against every port, releases unsent permits, records effect-uncertain and usage-uncertain outcomes and captures late receipts; a preview renderer that escapes hostile text in every surface, declares default-src 'none', makes zero external requests, refuses an unresolved section, node or source rather than omitting it, and draws a real directed SVG that says 'No relationship supplied' over an unconnected node -- the very honesty the shipped Polaris page's div-based figures cannot express. One check is the best idea in the package: the inventory stage's cited-source union must EQUAL the admitted source set, so the reviewer's denominator is the whole corpus and cannot be narrowed. But that is the only mechanical honesty in the loop. The provider schema has no field for Unknown, unresolved, inferred, omitted or quoted-versus-synthesised, while the shipped prompts instruct the model five times to use 'the supplied schema's unresolved/failure representation' and the adopted specification demands it three times -- so a model with no evidence has exactly two compliant moves, silence or invention, and a paragraph's [1] marker means only that a source id exists, never that the source says it. The edit and repair stages return the bare draft schema with no change list and no finding disposition, and no validator compares a stage's output to its input, so edit may silently delete supported claims and repair may ignore every finding -- after which the next review's denominator is recomputed from the shrunken draft, erasing the evidence of the deletion. The 'independent' fidelity review is the same provider route one stage later, holding the author's own plan, declaring coverage as two bare id lists with no per-entry disposition, and its verdict is the model's self-declared severity where zero findings means pass -- no evidence rendering green, in the one place VIS-2 matters most. And the loop has no owner and no exit: awaiting-rendered-review is terminal, the preview renders outside the pipeline, a CLI writes it to a directory, no daemon route serves it, no adapter connects PocModel.projectShape to the generator's provenance-free {sourceId, text} pairs, and the three owner acts bind the specification, never a generated word. Against 5,065 lines of adopted specification, 798 lines of design notes and 8.6 MB of approval evidence, the product loop has eight arrows and code for one and a half of them.

findings.title: The provider schema has no Unknown: the prompts instruct the model five times to use an unresolved representation that does not exist
findings.detail: ProviderParagraph is exactly {id, text, sourceIds}. A grep for unresolved/unknown/inferred/reason across provider-draft.ts returns only error-code strings ('unknown-source', 'unknown-node', 'unknown-section', 'unknown-finding-target') plus the plan section's free-text `reason`. There is no per-claim epistemic state, no produced/omitted/unresolved asset disposition, and no quotation-versus-synthesis marker anywhere in any of the six stage schemas. Meanwhile prompts.ts:6 tells every stage 'Follow the supplied schema's unresolved/failure representation when support or capability is missing', prompts.ts:13 requires 'the schema's disposition and a reason' for every requested asset, and prompts.ts:21 asks for 'unresolved reasons using the trusted schema'. The adopted spec is explicit: 'Source-supported inference SHALL expose its admitted premises and inferred status' (spec.md:52); 'The asset bundle SHALL distinguish source claims, supported inference and non-normative framing and preserve captured epistemic states' (spec.md:98); 'Each requested asset SHALL ... resolv[e] to one produced, omitted or unresolved disposition' (spec.md:1015). A model that lacks support therefore has no compliant way to say so: it omits (invisible) or it invents (indistinguishable). This is not a Phase-B integration gap -- requirements 002/003 are inside Phase A (EXECUTION-PHASES.md:18) and the schema is landed code.

findings.title: Edit and repair return the bare draft schema and no validator compares a stage's output to its input, so supported claims can vanish and findings can be ignored
findings.detail: provider-draft.ts:33 maps author, edit and repair to the identical `draft` schema. validateStage's else-branch (131-143) checks the plan, referential integrity of sourceIds, unique handles, section-set equality with the plan and diagram endpoints -- it never receives or consults the PRIOR draft. So the edit stage may return a draft with half the author's paragraphs removed and it validates. The consequence is worse than the deletion: pipeline.ts:262 overwrites context.draft, and the following fidelity stage's blockIds denominator is recomputed from the edited draft (provider-draft.ts:128), so the reviewer is never asked about the paragraphs that were dropped. The same hole sits under repair: pipeline.ts:267 passes findings in, gets a draft back, and nothing links any finding to any change -- a repair that returns its input unchanged passes validation, and if the next fidelity call happens to emit no blocking finding the run exits clean. The prompts ask for exactly the missing fields: 'report changed content and affected references using the supplied schema' (prompts.ts:18) and 'Return the schema's affected content and finding-to-change dispositions' (prompts.ts:22). The kit's own run contract names 'Concise, coherent revision plus change list' (README:65) and 'Bounded replacement artifacts' (README:67). No change list, no disposition and no replacement identity exists in the landed schema.

findings.title: The 'independent' review is the same provider route one stage later, holding the author's own plan, and its verdict is the model's self-declared severity
findings.detail: PipelineRequest carries a single scalar `providerRoute` (pipeline.ts:19) used for every stage, so the controller cannot structurally route fidelity to a different model, vendor or temperature even if an adapter wanted to -- independence is impossible by type, not merely unimplemented. pipeline.ts:263 calls stage('fidelity', context) where context (built at 170, extended at 259-262) holds sources, readerQuestions, inventory, plan AND draft: the reviewer receives the author's own argument plan, including each section's self-declared `reason`. Requirement 006 is explicit in the opposite direction: 'Reviewers SHALL receive the artifact, governing references and acceptance criteria without the authoring conversation' and 'The candidate-authoring stage SHALL NOT define or narrow its own review denominator' (spec.md:302). The pipeline hands over exactly what the fidelity prompt then asks the model to disregard ('Do not ... accept the author's self-assessment as evidence', prompts.ts:21) -- compliance by instruction where bounding by input was available and free. Finally reviewVerdict (provider-draft.ts:148-152) is `findings.some(f => f.severity === 'blocking')`: an empty findings array is a pass. The gate on the whole loop is the reviewed model's own opinion of its own severity, which is the precise shape VIS-2 forbids -- absence of evidence rendered as success.

findings.title: The fidelity coverage declaration is a checklist with no checkboxes: both coverage directions are bare id lists with no per-entry disposition
findings.detail: The fidelity schema (provider-draft.ts:30) is {inventoryIds: handle[], blockIds: handle[], findings: {severity,message,target}[]}. validateStage enforces that inventoryIds EQUALS the inventory's entry ids and blockIds EQUALS the draft's block ids (127-128) -- genuinely good denominator discipline, and the same discipline that makes inventory coverage real at 116. But an id list carries no verdict. The only way to say 'inventory entry 7 is absent from the draft' is a free-text finding with target='entry-7', and findings may be empty (minItems 0). So the mechanical content of the reviewer's coverage claim is 'I enumerated all of them', and the spec's requirement that the review 'SHALL record both inventory-to-draft coverage and draft-to-source support, including justified omissions; unresolved material omissions SHALL prevent readiness' (spec.md:302) is discharged entirely by model goodwill. The spec's own named scenario -- 'Source trade-off omitted entirely ... all generated claims have anchors but an independently inventoried material trade-off is absent ... THEN source-to-draft coverage records the omission as a blocking finding' (spec.md:325-329) -- has no field to record it in. Note also that `references()` (90-98) checks only that a cited sourceId EXISTS; nothing anywhere in the landed code ever compares a claim's text to the source text it cites. Referential integrity is being rendered as evidentiary support.

findings.title: The loop has no owner and no exit: awaiting-rendered-review is terminal, no route serves the preview, and no act binds generated output
findings.detail: Tracing the eight product arrows on main: (1) source reads -> extraction EXISTS, but only in the PWB pipeline, which the generator does not touch; (2) extraction -> generator MISSING (see L3-F6); (3) generator -> draft EXISTS (fixture-driven); (4) draft -> validation EXISTS but is referential only (F1-F4); (5) validation -> human review PROSE ONLY: pipeline.ts:272 returns status 'awaiting-rendered-review' and that status has no successor anywhere in the PipelineResult union (103-115) or in any consumer; the rendered preview is produced OUTSIDE the pipeline by pipeline-demo-main.ts:16, after the pipeline has already returned, so the fidelity reviewer that requirement 006 wants to see the rendering never can; (6) review -> adopted manifesto MISSING -- a grep of routes.ts for 'generation' or 'draft' returns zero hits, the daemon's route table is '/', '/api/poc', '/api/poc/polaris' plus the four human surfaces, and the only way to see a draft is `npm run poc:generator-demo -- --out <dir>` writing HTML to a directory; (7) adopted -> rendered Polaris page MISSING, and nothing links the two renderers; (8) owner tunes -> propagation MISSING. The three owner acts of 2026-09-12 bind the specification bytes and explicitly reserve effects ('Real-project reads, provider egress and destination writes remain separately admitted', ACT:42); nothing in the landed code produces an artifact an act could ever bind. Against doctrine's escape property -- intent changes must produce dispatched work -- 5,065 lines of adopted specification, 798 lines of design notes and 8.6 MB of approval evidence have so far produced 892 lines of code that dispatches nothing and no requirement end-to-end. This is honestly disclosed (PROJECT-STATUS.md:38-44, core README:65-67, tasks.md all-unchecked); the finding is the shape of the gap, not a concealment.

findings.title: The generator's source contract is provenance-free {sourceId, text}, and the observation plane is not connected to it at all; preview citations are array indices
findings.detail: A grep for three-surface-poc-core, PocModel or projectShape across packages/polaris-generation-core/src and apps/three-surface-poc/src/polaris-generation returns NONE. The two planes are entirely disjoint: the lawful reader (body-read-authority -> git-object-reader -> classification -> extraction -> coverage) produces a PocModel.projectShape carrying revision identity, evaluation instant, classification basis, exclusion state, exact-text spans and anchor identities -- and the generator's entire notion of a source is provider-draft.ts:109, `{sourceId: handle, text: string<=100000}`. Every one of those provenance fields is discarded at the type level, so even after adapters are written the generator cannot satisfy spec.md:98's requirement that 'Source anchors SHALL use the closed classes and durable revision/evaluation-bound identities required by RFC7-10, not labels or paths as identity'. The preview compounds it: draft-preview.ts:11 builds sourceId -> ARRAY INDEX and line 23 emits href='#source-N' with aria-label 'Read source N' -- the citation identity is a position in the caller's array, so reordering the input silently renumbers every citation on the page. Today pipeline-demo.ts:33-37 hand-writes three string literals as the entire source corpus and verifySources is `async () => true` (line 67). The fix is not an adapter bolted onto this type; it is a richer type.

findings.title: Every stage re-sends the whole accumulated context against one cumulative budget, so the admitted corpus is re-billed five to six times and hard caps bound the corpus the generator can ever accept
findings.detail: context starts as {sources, readerQuestions} (170) and each stage receives the WHOLE object (259-263): plan sees sources+inventory, author sees +plan, edit sees +draft, fidelity sees all five, repair sees all five plus findings. Each stage's envelope is encoded whole and charged against a single cumulative scalar, `inputBytes + size > budget.maxInputBytes` (176-179), and the envelope also embeds a full copy of the system prompt that is separately passed as `system` at line 219, so the prompt is billed twice per call. [Observed] Butlers at 7c8743f63 reports 278 sources with 86 bodies read totalling 1,120,065 bytes (api-poc.json projectShape.resourceUse.totalBytes / counts.sources). Sending that corpus through the landed chain costs roughly 6.5 MB of provider input before a single drafted word exists, and maxInputBytes must simultaneously be large enough to encode the whole request in one canonical pass (pipeline.ts:143). There is no source selection, no retrieval, no per-stage scoping. Two hard caps also bound what can ever be admitted: `list()` defaults maxItems to 200 (provider-draft.ts:15) and the source list uses that default (109), so a project with more than 200 admitted bodies is refused outright; and because the inventory's cited-source union must EQUAL the source set (116) while entries are also capped at 200, a 200-source project gets exactly one inventory claim per source with no room for a second.

findings.title: Resume is forbidden by the port contract, and a repair cannot add or remove a section, so the spec's own 'omitted trade-off' scenario is mechanically unrepairable
findings.detail: The admit port's contract says 'An already-dispatched identity MUST refuse; lease expiry cannot replay it' (pipeline.ts:62-64), and pipeline.test.ts:74-75 pins the behaviour: re-running the same request returns admission-refused at stage 0. Combined with runGenerationPipeline always entering at 'inventory' (line 259), idempotency and resume are mutually exclusive by design: a run that dies at fidelity discards four paid stages, and re-running under a fresh requestId re-pays all of them. Requirement 008 ('Safe resume and duplicate requests') is a Phase A obligation (EXECUTION-PHASES.md:18), so this is a landed interface that forecloses a Phase A requirement, not merely an unbuilt one. Separately, the draft validator pins the section set to the author's plan -- `same([...sections], unique(plan.sections.map(s => s.id)))` (provider-draft.ts:137) -- and the repair stage uses that same branch. A blocking finding of the exact kind the spec names, 'an independently inventoried material trade-off is absent from the account' (spec.md:325-329), typically needs a new section; the repair stage cannot produce one, so the loop can only spin to repair-exhausted (pipeline.ts:266). The plan stage is never re-entered.

findings.title: The one regeneration test is tautological: it compares digests of two scripted fixtures built from the changed string
findings.detail: The test named 'binds changed source meaning to fresh inventory, draft and fidelity inputs' asserts that inputDigests differ between two runs and that the author outputDigest differs. Both are necessarily true: pipeline-demo.ts:38-57 derives the scripted inventory, plan, draft and review mechanically from the project object, so changing project.qualification changes the fixture, and the digest difference tests the hash function rather than any regeneration semantics. The same shape appears in the CLI's third case (pipeline-demo-main.ts:12, `${first.qualification} Outdoor care also depends on the season.`). This is disclosed honestly in the emitted report.json ('realProvider': false, 'realProjectProof': false, pipeline-demo-main.ts:21-25) and in the core README's 'Still required' list, so the defect is the test's name promising more than its assertion, not a false evidence claim. Worth renaming before it is ever cited as source-drift coverage for task 3.3.

moves.title: Give the provider schema somewhere to put Unknown, and make omission impossible to express by silence
moves.what: Add to every claim-bearing node a required `support` discriminant -- {kind: 'quoted', sourceId, span} | {kind: 'synthesis', sourceIds[]} | {kind: 'inference', premiseIds[], inferredFrom} | {kind: 'unresolved', reason} -- replacing the bare sourceIds array. Add a required per-asset disposition {produced|omitted|unresolved, reason} to diagrams, deep dives and tables, and an `unresolved: {question, reason}[]` array at draft level whose minItems is not zero when the plan requested something the sources could not support. Make renderDraftPreview render each kind differently: a quotation as exact text, an inference with its premises named, an unresolved node as a visible Unknown with its reason -- never as a footnote number.
moves.why: This is the one change that separates a draft that CAN be honest from one that structurally cannot. Today a model with no evidence must omit or invent, and the reader cannot tell a verbatim promise from a fabricated one because both render as `text [1]`. VIS-2 says no evidence means Unknown; the landed schema has no Unknown. The adopted specification already requires all three pieces (spec.md:52, :98, :1015) and the shipped prompts already instruct the model to use them, so this is closing a contradiction inside landed bytes rather than extending scope.
slice_plan: Define the support discriminant and asset disposition in provider-draft.ts; bump every stage schema version to -v2.

Teach validateStage that an 'inference' support must name premise ids that resolve to inventory entries, and that 'quoted' spans must be substrings of the named source text -- the first mechanical entailment check in the package.
Render the four kinds distinctly in draft-preview.ts, with an Unknown treatment copied from the PWB renderer's vocabulary rather than invented.
Add a counterexample test per kind: a fabricated quotation whose span is absent from its source must fail validation, and a mutation of the substring check must fail (rule 6).

moves.title: Turn the fidelity coverage declaration into a per-entry disposition and make the verdict a function of the denominator, not of the model's mood
moves.what: Replace `inventoryIds: handle[]` with `inventoryCoverage: {entryId, disposition: 'represented'|'justified-omission'|'unsupported'|'unresolved', blockIds[], reason}[]` and `blockIds: handle[]` with `blockSupport: {blockId, verdict: 'supported'|'anchor-does-not-support'|'unresolved', sourceIds[], reason}[]`. Keep the existing set-equality checks so both remain whole-population. Then make reviewVerdict block on any entry whose disposition is not 'represented' or 'justified-omission', any block whose verdict is not 'supported', AND any missing row -- so silence blocks instead of passing.
moves.why: This flips the single most consequential polarity in the loop. Today zero findings equals ready, which is VIS-2 inverted at the exact gate the product depends on; afterwards, readiness requires a positive disposition for every row of a denominator the model cannot narrow. It also gives requirement 006's named 'omitted trade-off' scenario a field to be recorded in, and gives the owner something to read: a coverage table, not a verdict word.
slice_plan: Extend the fidelity schema and keep same() on both id sets, now derived from the disposition rows.
Rewrite reviewVerdict as fail-closed over the rows; delete the severity-only path.

Test: a review with every row present and one 'unsupported' blocks; a review with a missing row is invalid-output, not a pass; a review with zero findings and a complete 'represented' set passes. Mutate each predicate.

moves.title: Make edit and repair account for what they changed, and forbid silent deletion
moves.what: Give the edit and repair stages their own response schemas (not `draft`): a changed-block list {blockId, action: 'kept'|'rewritten'|'split'|'removed', reason, newBlockIds[]} covering every block id of the input draft, plus for repair a finding-to-change disposition {findingId, action: 'repaired'|'unrepairable', reason, affectedBlockIds[]} covering every supplied finding. Pass the prior draft into validateStage for these stages and enforce total coverage of prior block ids. Allow the repair stage to re-enter the plan stage when a finding requires a section the plan does not have.
moves.why: Today edit can delete a supported claim and the next review's denominator is recomputed from the shrunken draft, so the deletion is not merely unreported -- it is unreportable. Repair can ignore every finding and the loop can still exit clean. Both prompts already ask for exactly these fields and the kit's run contract already names them; only the schema is missing. Re-entering the plan is what makes the spec's own named repair scenario mechanically possible.
slice_plan: Split `edit` and `repair` out of the shared `draft` schema entry at provider-draft.ts:33.
Thread priorDraft into validateStage's context for those stages; enforce total prior-block coverage.
Relax the plan pin at line 137 to 'sections must match the CURRENT plan', and let a repair emit a plan revision that re-runs validation.
Counterexample test: an edit output missing one prior block id must be invalid-output; mutate the coverage check and confirm the test fails.

moves.title: Make independence structural: per-stage provider routes, and a fidelity envelope that cannot contain the authoring conversation
moves.what: Replace PipelineRequest.providerRoute with routes: Record<GenerationStage, string> so the fidelity and author stages can be different models or vendors, and build the fidelity stage's envelope explicitly from {sources, inventory, draft, acceptanceCriteria} rather than passing the accumulated context -- dropping `plan` and `readerQuestions-as-authored`. Record the fidelity route and model identity on the receipt so the owner can see WHO reviewed.
moves.why: Requirement 006 says reviewers receive the artifact and criteria 'without the authoring conversation', and the landed code hands over the author's own plan and then instructs the model by prompt to ignore it. Bounding the input costs nothing and cannot be talked out of. The single scalar route also means today's architecture could not use a second model even if one were admitted -- fixing the type now is far cheaper than after adapters exist.
slice_plan: Change providerRoute to a per-stage map; thread it into AttemptInput and the receipt.
Construct each stage's inputs explicitly at the call site instead of reusing the mutating `context` object.
Test that the fidelity envelope's encoded bytes contain no plan handle, by asserting on the canonical encoding rather than by reading the prompt.

moves.title: Type the generator's source as an observation, not a string pair, and make citations durable identities
moves.what: Replace {sourceId, text} with the observation identity the PWB pipeline already produces: {sourceId, path, revision, evaluation, classificationBasis, exclusionState, spans: {anchorId, start, end, text}[]}. Have the model cite anchorIds, not array positions, and have renderDraftPreview resolve every citation through the anchor identity into the existing exact-source route rather than `#source-N`. Excluded and path-only sources appear in the corpus as first-class Unknowns rather than being dropped before the generator sees them.
moves.why: This is the bridge between the two planes and the prerequisite for every real run. It also closes the preview's positional-citation defect (reordering the input renumbers every citation) and lets the generator inherit, rather than re-invent, the one thing Polaris is already world-class at: anchored exact text. Without it the generator can never satisfy spec.md:98's RFC7-10 anchor obligation no matter how good the adapters are.
slice_plan: Define the observation-shaped source type in polaris-generation-core, with no import from three-surface-poc-core (keep the core project-neutral).
Write one adapter in the app that projects PocModel.projectShape into it -- the first arrow between the planes.
Change draft-preview citations to anchor identities and reuse verbatim-route's href construction.
Test that shuffling the source array does not change a single rendered citation.

moves.title: Prove the loop on Syzygy's own corpus with a scripted provider before asking for egress
moves.what: Using L3-M5's adapter, run the unchanged pipeline over Syzygy's own governed corpus (its doctrine, decisions and contracts are already readable without any consent act) with a deterministic local 'provider' that is a scripted or rule-based responder, and publish the resulting draft preview as the second project. Then perturb one governed file and regenerate, checking that exactly the affected blocks, diagrams and citations move.
moves.why: Task 3.3 demands two materially different real projects and a changed-source regeneration, and both are currently blocked on consent and egress acts the owner has not been asked for. Syzygy is a real project whose sources need neither. Running against it exercises every portability assumption -- real path shapes, real source counts, real contradictions -- and will find the input-budget and 200-source ceilings (L3-F7) before an egress act is spent discovering them. It is also the cheapest possible answer to 'would this work on a second repository today?'.
slice_plan: Point the M5 adapter at the Syzygy tree behind an explicit test-only profile; no new read authority is needed.
Replace the scripted responses with a deterministic rule-based responder so the stage contracts are exercised at real scale.
Record the budget and cap breaches honestly as findings rather than tuning the fixture until it fits.
Overlaps L1-M5 (self-profile for the OBSERVER); this is the generator-input analogue and should share the profile if L1-M5 lands first.

moves.title: Serve the draft at a route, and make the owner's one lawful action a drafted act
moves.what: Add GET /polaris/draft/<runId> to the daemon serving renderDraftPreview's output beside the coverage table from L3-M2, with the run's receipts, budget spend and the stage that produced each block. Add one owner control -- accept / reject / repair-this-block -- whose accept path emits a DRAFTED act packet (subject digest, phrase, manifest) to a file for the owner to perform out of band, never a performed act.
moves.why: Today the loop terminates at a status with no successor: the preview reaches a directory on disk and no further. Doctrine's escape property says intent changes must produce dispatched work, and VIS-4 says only owner sign-off binds -- a drafted-never-performed act packet satisfies both. This is the first arrow that puts the owner inside the generation loop at all. Overlaps L2-M3 (one click from an Unknown to a drafted owner act) in mechanism; keep them unified rather than building two packet writers.
slice_plan: Add the route behind the existing boundedResponse ceiling; a draft preview is small enough that the P0-CEILING problem does not recur.
Render the L3-M2 coverage table above the draft, so the reader sees the denominator before the prose.
Emit the drafted packet through the existing recorder conventions; never call a recorder's perform path.
Extend the PipelineResult union with the states after awaiting-rendered-review so the type shows the loop's real shape.

moves.title: Make regeneration cheap: stage-scoped inputs, resumable attempts, and a drift band on the rendered page
moves.what: Three coupled changes. (a) Stop resending the whole corpus: after the inventory stage, downstream stages receive the inventory plus only the source spans their inputs cite, and sources are billed once. (b) Split `admit` into reserve/complete so a completed attempt identity returns its recorded artifact instead of refusing, making a run resumable at the stage it died on. (c) Bind each published manifesto to its snapshotId and render a drift band -- 'generated at snapshot X; the project is now at Y; N of M cited sources changed' -- with a one-click regenerate that reuses unaffected stage artifacts.
moves.why: Regeneration is the difference between a manifesto and a report. Today a Butlers run costs roughly 6.5 MB of provider input (L3-F7), cannot resume (L3-F8), and nothing on any page would ever tell the owner that the manifesto has gone stale. (a) and (b) together make the recurring operation affordable; (c) makes it something the owner is prompted to do rather than something they must remember. Overlaps L2-M6's evaluation-delta rendering -- share the retained-evaluation store rather than building a second one.
slice_plan: Construct per-stage inputs explicitly (shares the refactor with L3-M4) and charge sources once.
Change the admit contract to reserve/complete with a recorded-artifact return; keep the replay prohibition for IN-FLIGHT identities only.
Store snapshotId + cited anchor digests with each published draft; compute the drift band at render time from the current evaluation.
Test resume by killing a run at fidelity and confirming the rerun pays only the fidelity stage.

moves.title: Name the egress act the loop is waiting on, and state what it buys
moves.what: Prepare, but do not perform, the provider-egress owner offer: which content class leaves the machine, to which route, under what retention, with what refusal on withdrawal -- and attach to it the concrete evidence that everything buildable without egress has been built (M1-M6). State explicitly in PROJECT-STATUS that no model has been called and that the honesty layer, not the provider, is the current critical path.
moves.why: Provider egress is the single act gating every real quality obligation in tasks.md section 3, and it is the one thing no amount of engineering can substitute for. But asking for it now would buy a real model output that the current validators cannot check (F1-F4), spending owner trust on a run whose honesty is unverifiable. Sequencing the ask after the honesty layer means the first real call is also the first checkable one. L5-agent-consumer.label: L5-agent-consumer
L5-agent-consumer.gap: Judged from inside a coding agent starting a task on Butlers, Syzygy is a very good observation record with no briefing, no dispatch and no return path. The credentialed machine channel is 5,508,208 bytes of which the agent's whole orientation -- evaluation identity, consent scope, authority acts, the nine-node propagation graph, the one proposed change, the exclusions, the counts, the readiness verdict -- is 18,710 bytes (0.340%); 97.3% of the transfer is 7,396 Butlers beads and 6,466 file paths, the two blocks least scoped to any task. What it then cannot answer is the question the agent actually has: for openspec/specs/switchboard-identity/spec.md -- the spec the whole three-state demonstration turns on -- /api/poc returns 511 bytes carrying a path, a line number, a folder name and 'Observed report-fact fresh unchallenged', and no requirement text at all; the only channel that discloses requirement text is /polaris/source, credentialClass 'human-open', HTML-only, gated on a browser-origin check -- so the authenticated machine channel is the thin one and the substantive one is unauthenticated markup. The escape property is invisible on that channel entirely: 'externalRef', 'governingIntent' and 'syzygy-poc:work:' occur zero times in the payload, because the materialization packet -- the one dispatch artifact in the system -- exists only as a <dl> inside a Trajectory <form>. Underneath sits a deeper type problem: PocEpistemic is a two-member union {Observed,basis}|{Unknown,reason} of free prose with no tier, freshness, challenge or route, and it governs every entity and every edge of intent->work->code->evidence, while ProjectShapeClaim carries the full tuple beside it -- so the payload holds three epistemic shapes and the weakest one owns the propagation axis. And the vocabulary member reserved for agent output is unreachable: EPISTEMIC_LABELS declares Observed/Inferred/Unknown, the legend defines 'asserted-by-worker -- stated by an agent, not read; always Inferred', doctrine says an LLM assertion is Inferred never Observed, and no POC production module can construct an Inferred claim. An agent's result therefore has no representable state, which is why the round trip -- whose two halves are already built and lawful (POST /trajectory/materialize, and npm run poc:capture-test-artifact writing a safe-field TestArtifactRecord outside the daemon per SEC-3) -- has never been run end to end and the V0 agent-consumption test's artifact does not exist. Tier is weak rather than broken because the primitives are unusually good: identity.scope states the consented content class machine-legibly, authority[] names each act identity and digest with its own independence disclosure, proposedWork is a genuine 2,278-byte briefing object for one hard-coded change, and RFC8-21 already specifies the eight-link return chain as accepted contract. Nothing here needs inventing; it needs serving, typing and running once.

L6-cross-surface.label: L6-cross-surface
L6-cross-surface.gap: Judged as one product with three surfaces over three states, Syzygy is four pages that share a stylesheet, a nav bar and a storage location, and almost nothing else. Counted this session: each of the four served pages carries exactly four cross-surface hrefs — /, /polaris, /trajectory, /orrery — and all four sit in the shared site-nav, so of 1,439 hrefs across the four captures, zero go from a claim to the same subject on another surface, although every surface already mints a per-claim fragment id that would serve as the target. The four renderers read four disjoint slices of PocModel and no field is read by all four; the model's own surfaces declaration says Polaris presents 4 entities while the page presents 415 items, and only the home page reads that declaration. The home page — the literal referent of the north star's 'open one place' — is governed by no requirement in the signed-off spec, still says 'One capability. Three honest views.', and names as its subject a capability that occupies 2.0% of the Polaris page it links to. The words desired, execution and observed appear together once across all four pages, inside a disclaimer. And the one cross-cutting invariant that IS in force, POC-REQ-060, is falsified on the surface with 699 of the POC's claims: Polaris renders Observed and Unknown in the same grey .claim-tuple with no selector keyed on the label, uses the legend's declared badge exactly twice — both inside the legend — and its checker sets its denominator to four pages against a population of 1,085 encodings, passing on a substring the legend alone supplies. What is genuinely strong underneath: the addresses already exist on every surface, POC-REQ-053 already states the exact oracle a cross-surface resolvability requirement would need, and the deferral that produced this gap (RFC6-1/6-3/6-12) was recorded deliberately and honestly, so closing it is an owner act rather than a repair.

findings.title: The home route is governed by no requirement, while the cross-surface identity system is a declared deferral
findings.detail: The signed-off spec covers Polaris (030-032), Trajectory (040-043), Orrery (050-053) and two cross-cutting invariants (060 design language, 061 accessibility). It says nothing about '/' — the page the owner opens first and the literal referent of the north star's 'open one place'. No requirement, no falsifier, no Unknown discipline of its own. Separately, CONTRACT-COVERAGE.md records RFC6-1 ('POC builds no cross-surface selection/identity system'), RFC6-3 ('no navigable selection system') and RFC6-12 ('no shared URL-selection system across surfaces') as deliberate deferrals. So L6-F2 and L6-F4 are not defects against this spec — they are the deferral's consequence now arriving, and closing them is a spec-amendment act, not a bug fix. The shape to generalize already exists in POC-REQ-053: 'two projections of one graph … zero dangling links over the exhausted population'. [Observed]

Today Polaris promises a cyan ● and an amber ? in a legend it then uses twice, and renders its 699 real claim states — Observed and Unknown alike — in one grey. The owner reading the manifesto cannot see epistemic state at a glance on the one surface that has 699 of them. The check that would catch it measures four pages by substring presence and is satisfied by the legend. This is the highest-value/lowest-cost item in this lens: it is an in-force requirement, currently falsified, with the falsifier already written down.
